lines.text: Amazon sells 5 quarts of full synthetic for under 20 bucks so can it really beat Mobil 1?
So he freezes all 3 oils at minus 15 degrees for 24 hours and races them down a ramp.
Because a cold engine needs oil flowing right away or the moving parts run dry.
beats: ai:frosty car engine bay on a frozen winter morning with ice crystals on the metal
ai:macro of two steel engine parts rubbing with a very thin film of amber oil

lines.text: And the cheap Amazon oil hits the bottom first and beats Mobil 1 by 2 inches.
While Valvoline's conventional oil lands 6 inches behind so synthetic clearly flows better in the cold.
beats: ai:two glass tubes of motor oil side by side one flowing freely one thick and sluggish in frosty air

lines.text: But on the wear tester Mobil 1 leaves the smallest scar on the bearing.
Its scar is about 9 percent smaller than Amazon's.
But Amazon beats Valvoline by 17 percent which is wild for the price.
Then he cooks each oil at 400 degrees for 2 hours because that's how hot it gets near the piston rings.
beats: ai:cutaway of a glowing hot engine piston with its metal rings inside a cylinder

lines.text: Valvoline loses 3 grams to vapor while both synthetics lose just 1 gram which is oil that would vanish from your engine.
beats: ai:close up of a car engine oil dipstick pulled out showing a low oil level

lines.text: After cooking he freezes them again and Amazon still wins so the cheap oil holds up under heat.
So would you put 20 dollar oil in your car?
